newsitem.title: EGYPT: Saddam's son may go abroad for treatment - paper.
newsitem.headline: Saddam's son may go abroad for treatment - paper.

text.p: The Iraqi authorities have ordered a medivac plane to take President Saddam Hussein's son Uday to Switzerland for treatment after he was shot last week, the international Arabic newspaper al-Hayat said on Monday.

Uday was wounded in a Baghdad street last Thursday night in an attack for which two opposition groups in exile have claimed responsibility. The Iraqi government says it is investigating but it has not identified the gunmen.

Al-Hayat, which is based in London, also quoted Arab sources in London as saying that a woman travelling in the same car as Uday was killed in the attack and that the Iraqis were looking into the possibility that another woman may have told the gunmen where Uday would be that evening.
It said that the Iraqis were arresting relatives of Saddam Hussein's son-in-law Hussein Kamel, who was killed in Baghdad earlier this year shortly after returning from exile.
Uday is being treated at Ibn Sina hospital in Baghdad and according to official accounts his wounds are not serious.
Youth Television, which is owned by Uday, said on Sunday that Uday had telephoned the Iraqi soccer team in Dubai to wish them well in the Asian Cup.
But in the four days since the attack the Iraqi media have not shown pictures of him or offered any other conclusive evidence that he is still alive.
